incidents.victim: Apollo Global Management (and wider private equity, law and finance sector)
incidents.vector: Voice-phishing and social engineering of staff (impersonating IT support) to gain access to cloud platforms.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed Apollo cloud systems July 6-10, exposing names, dates of birth, addresses and Social Security numbers; part of a broader extortion wave hitting private equity firms, law firms, rating agencies and medtech, with competitors Blackstone and Bain Capital also reportedly targeted.

incidents.vector: Claimed data theft traced by the bank to a compromise of a contractor to one of its third-party vendors (a fourth-party incident).
incidents.impact: A ransomware gang added U.S. Bancorp to its leak site and threatened to publish data within two weeks; the bank says its own systems, networks and data repositories show no evidence of compromise and attributes the claims to an event outside its environment.

incidents.vector: Data theft believed tied to a third-party software application; briefly took down the hospital's careers website.
incidents.impact: Personal information of current and former employees, job applicants and staff of related organizations including the SickKids Foundation was likely stolen; no clinical systems or patient data affected. Affected individuals offered two years of credit monitoring.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the national road traffic agency's databases (vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: Personal details of 1.2 million Latvian citizens stolen, including payment receipts and license plate data going back to 2008; authorities warned of follow-on scams and the CSDD leadership resigned.

incidents.victim: Web servers in government, education, media, technology and gaming (global)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese-speaking (data theft & SEO fraud)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known one-day vulnerabilities (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro) for RCE on internet-facing IIS and Linux servers, with agentic AI automating exploitation, reconnaissance and payload generation.
incidents.impact: Financially motivated group tracked as a Chinese-speaking crew compromised servers across Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam for SEO fraud and data theft, deploying the new cross-platform SPECTRE implant with a Linux rootkit and BYOVD EDR-killing capabilities; a target list of ~170,000 URLs was recovered.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with regionally tailored Office documents, sometimes in password-protected RAR archives, that trigger a macro chain to deploy remote access Trojans.
incidents.impact: A China-nexus espionage operation targeted government entities in Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan using seven RAT families (five previously undocumented), running command channels over trusted services like Google Drive to maintain long-term access as China expands influence in the region.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators (Siemens S7 PLC users)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning to find exposed Siemens S7 PLCs, then AI-generated Python exploit scripts using the snap7 library and S7comm protocol, disguised as legitimate monitoring tools, to read/write PLC memory and logic.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned of an active threat conducting persistent reconnaissance and capability development against S7-200/300/400/1200/1500 PLCs in Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water, Chemical, Food & Agriculture and Commercial Facilities, assessed as pre-positioning for future operational effects against critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Hardware supply-chain backdoor: NERO R-ONE speed cameras (rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M units) execute malicious code delivered via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers.
incidents.impact: Slovakia's NBU security service flagged 279 EU-funded cameras bought through a Cyprus shell company as containing a Russian backdoor and multiple insecurities (SecureBoot off, unauthenticated live streams); the Interior Ministry paused deployment pending an independent audit.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident affecting the health-records provider (vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: Electronic health records giant CareCloud disclosed that 3.7 million people were impacted by a March 2026 cybersecurity incident; one of several healthcare breaches disclosed in the same week.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access exposing patient and employee data (vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: Baylor Genetics is notifying individuals of a June 2026 breach that exposed medical testing information, laboratory test results, health insurance data and Social Security numbers for both patients and employees.

incidents.victim: Fortune 500 enterprises (McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap, hotel chains)
incidents.vector: Compromised credentials used with MFA-fatigue and password-spraying to access victims' Microsoft Entra (Azure) tenants; specific intrusion vector unverified.
incidents.impact: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claimed a large-scale Azure exfiltration campaign (Aug 1-17), offering to sell employee and enterprise data from roughly a dozen major companies including McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl and hotel chains; claims not independently verified by researchers.

incidents.victim: Government, healthcare and critical infrastructure organizations (global)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing devices, including Fortinet FortiOS/FortiProxy auth-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472) and exposed VPN/RDP.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, DC3, NSA, USSS and Korea's KNPA issued a joint advisory on Gunra, a Conti-derived double-extortion ransomware-as-a-service that expanded its affiliate program in 2026 and hit victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific in healthcare, finance, manufacturing and government.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure, healthcare and other sectors (500+ victims)
incidents.vector: Phishing for credentials and rapid exploitation of newly disclosed CVEs (including Fortra GoAnywhere CVE-2025-10035 and BeyondTrust CVE-2026-1731), often within 24 hours of disclosure.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA and HHS updated the Medusa ransomware-as-a-service advisory, reporting the double-extortion operation has now impacted over 500 victims as of April 2026, with the Healthcare and Public Health sector a frequent target.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of multiple SharePoint RCE and auth-bypass vulnerabilities, followed by theft of IIS machine keys and deserialization attacks for persistence and malware deployment.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-55040 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and updated hardening guidance, warning that all supported on-premises SharePoint versions are under active exploitation enabling unauthorized access and persistent post-exploitation footholds.

incidents.victim: Companies hiring remote technical staff (1,100+ firms)
incidents.vector: Fraudulent employment: operators use fabricated personas, AI-generated profile photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI interview tools to secure remote jobs, aided by facilitators who host company hardware.
incidents.impact: Recorded Future detailed 'PurpleDelta' clusters of North Korean IT workers (likely based in China) that applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely employed at 10+, posing an ongoing insider-threat and revenue channel for the DPRK regime; a U.S. federal agency was separately reported to have unknowingly hired a DPRK remote worker.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) flooding.
incidents.impact: An Iranian hacktivist group calling itself the '313 Team' claimed DDoS attacks that caused prolonged outages at Bluesky and GitHub over consecutive days; the same group ran a similar wave in April.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting building-management and access-control systems.
incidents.impact: A ransomware attack disabled access doors and heating, ventilation and air conditioning at Winnipeg's largest hospital, forcing increased on-site security while the access-card system was down; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Government networks in Taiwan and Thailand
incidents.vector: Publicly available AI agent frameworks used to automate reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement and data exfiltration in a near-autonomous intrusion.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese hackers used AI tooling to breach Taiwanese government networks and Thailand's Ministry of Finance as part of a wave hitting multiple Asian governments, described by researchers as among the first near-autonomous AI-driven attacks on government targets.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT administrators and their managed networks
incidents.vector: Fake job interviews: victims contacted via Telegram and asked to download 'test' applications that deploy Windows or Linux malware.
incidents.impact: A Sandworm sub-unit (tracked as UAC-0145) inside Russia's GRU has, since May 2026, targeted Ukrainian system administrators and IT professionals with fake recruitment lures to harvest credentials and pivot into networks they manage for intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into corporate systems followed by publication of stolen customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: A breach at French shipping and logistics firm CEVA disrupted freight delivery across much of Europe and leaked customer data; affected businesses include Valve's Steam hardware operation and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf, which warned of days- to weeks-long delivery delays.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of an XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the application.
incidents.impact: Hackers claimed to have breached MyDr, a platform used by Polish hospitals that reportedly stores data on nearly 19 million Poles, stealing customer files and source code now offered for sale; Polish authorities are investigating.

incidents.victim: WilmerHale and Goodwin Procter (U.S. law firms)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing and social engineering to gain access, followed by data-theft extortion.
incidents.impact: Two of the largest U.S. law firms paid multi-million-dollar ransoms this year — WilmerHale at least $18 million and Goodwin Procter $10 million — to Luna Moth (Silent Ransom Group), which specializes in extorting law firms.
